title: Trigger and Resolve a Real Merge Conflict
description: Create two conflicting edits to the exact same line of `hello.txt` on two different branches, trigger a conflict, resolve it, and commit.
steps: In `hcc-git-practice`, make sure you are on `main`: `git switch main`
Edit line 1 of `hello.txt` to say: 'Hello from Developer Alice!' — stage and commit: `git commit -am "alice: update greeting"`
Edit line 1 of `hello.txt` to say: 'Hello from Developer Bob!' — stage and commit: `git commit -am "bob: update greeting"`
Switch back to `main` and merge branch A: `git switch main && git merge conflict-a` (merges cleanly!)
Now attempt to merge branch B into `main`: `git merge conflict-b` — BOOM! Conflict detected!
Open `hello.txt` in VS Code or your editor — inspect `<<<<<<< HEAD`, `=======`, `>>>>>>> conflict-b`
Edit the file to choose the best greeting (or keep both), remove ALL conflict marker lines, and save
Stage the resolved file: `git add hello.txt`
Complete the merge commit: `git commit -m "merge: resolve greeting conflict between Alice and Bob"`
Delete the test branches: `git branch -d conflict-a conflict-b`
expected_output: `git status` confirms clean working tree and `git log --oneline` shows a successful merge commit.
tips: If you ever get overwhelmed during a merge conflict, run `git merge --abort` to return everything to the exact state before the merge!
Never leave conflict marker lines (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`) in your code — they will cause syntax errors in your application.
